title: Finite quotient reduction preserves the finite constructible categories
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $r\geq m\geq1$, $A_r=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ and $A_m=\mathbf Z/\ell^m\mathbf Z$. Let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for the comparison from the ordinary etale to the pro-etale derived category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $K$ have bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, where $a\leq b$ are integers [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Let $K_0$ be a bounded constructible ordinary-etale complex with a specified isomorphism $C_TK_0\cong K$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Then $K_0$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and has a representative $Q$ consisting of flat etale $A_r$-module sheaves, zero outside $[a,b]$. Both $Q$ over $A_r$ and $Q\otimes_{A_r}A_m$ over $A_m$ are K-flat (tensoring with them preserves acyclic complexes). The latter represents $K_0\otimes^L_{A_r}A_m$ and is zero outside $[a,b]$. The complex $K\otimes^L_{A_r}A_m$ has bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ over $A_m$, and its bounded constructible ordinary-etale origin is $K_0\otimes^L_{A_r}A_m$, through the canonical comparison
$$C_T(K_0\otimes^L_{A_r}A_m)\cong K\otimes^L_{A_r}A_m.$$
For $r\geq m\geq n\geq1$, these comparisons commute with the derived tensor associator; on the flat model the associator is $(q\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto q\otimes bc$. No flatness of $A_m$ over $A_r$ is assumed.

source.place: Coefficient extension on bounded flat models; intrinsic finite-Tor and constructibility checks

proof.text: Write $C_r$ and $C_m$ for the comparison functors with the indicated coefficients. The given $K_0$ is bounded, hence belongs to $D^+(T_{\mathrm{Et}},A_r)$. Apply [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] with the finite commutative ring $A_r$. Its reverse implication and the specified isomorphism $C_rK_0\cong K$ give Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for $K_0$. This tests all ordinary-etale module sheaves, exactly as required; no hypothesis about a finite-type base field is introduced.

source.place: First paragraph: bounded flat models; Tor amplitude reflected to the etale origin

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-etale-flat-model] to $K_0$, using its given bounded constructibility and $a\leq b$. Obtain a complex $Q$ of flat etale $A_r$-module sheaves, zero outside $[a,b]$, with $Q\cong K_0$ in the derived category. Since $Q$ is bounded above, [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes it K-flat. Only flat terms are claimed: the theorem used here imposes no Noetherian hypothesis on $T$, and we do not require the terms of $Q$ to be constructible.

Set $Q_m=Q\otimes_{A_r}A_m$ termwise, on the etale site. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] to the map of constant ring sheaves $(A_r)_T\to(A_m)_T$: $Q_m$ has flat $A_m$-terms and is K-flat over $A_m$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] it represents $L_m=K_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_r}A_m$ in the derived category of $A_m$-modules. The term in degree $i$ is $Q^i\otimes_{A_r}A_m$, hence is zero for $i\notin[a,b]$. These results require no flatness of $A_m$ as an $A_r$-module.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, applied to identity of topoi with coefficient map; Tags 06YT and 06YV, derived change of rings

proof.text: For every etale $A_m$-module sheaf $N$, K-flatness computes $L_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_m}N$ by $Q_m\otimes_{A_m}N$, which has zero terms outside $[a,b]$. Thus $L_m$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$. Taking $N=(A_m)_T$ also shows that $L_m$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. This is the definition [def-kun-tor-amplitude] and the computation in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], applied now to $A_m$ and the identity coefficient map.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude; Tag 08G1, lemma-tor-amplitude, direction (2) implies (1)

proof.text:
Write $C_r,C_m$ as in Step 1. Part (1) of [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] identifies $
u_T^{-1}(A_r)_T$ and $
u_T^{-1}(A_m)_T$ with the pro-etale constant rings, compatibly with $A_r	o A_m$, and the module inverse image with $
u_T^{-1}$; by parts (2)-(3) $C_r,C_m$ are termwise exact, so $C_mL_m$ is represented by $C_m(Q\otimes_{A_r}A_m)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], applied to the inclusion of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] (it preserves finite limits and coverings), $
u_T^{-1}$ preserves all colimits and $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$. Since $Q^i\otimes_{A_r}A_m$ is the coequalizer of the two action maps $Q^i\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A_r\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A_mightrightarrows Q^i\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A_m$, this gives a termwise isomorphism of complexes $C_m(Q\otimes_{A_r}A_m)\cong C_rQ\otimes_{A_r}A_m$, sending $
u^{-1}(q\otimes b)$ to $
u^{-1}q\otimes b$ on local sections and commuting with the differentials, which act on $q$ only. It is $A_r$-linear, hence $A_m$-linear, because local sections of $A_m$ lift through the surjection $A_r	woheadrightarrow A_m$. On the other side, $C_rQ\cong C_rK_0\cong K$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_r)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] (with $u=
u_T$, $R=S=A_r$) makes $C_rQ$ K-flat with flat terms. Hence [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the pro-etale site says that $C_rQ\otimes_{A_r}A_m$ represents $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_r}A_m$. Composing,
$$C_mL_m\cong C_rQ\otimes_{A_r}A_m\cong K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_r}A_m$$
in $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_m)$, not just after forgetting to $A_r$. The termwise map is natural in chain maps, and the canonicity clause of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes the comparison independent of the flat model. All sites are small skeletons in the common larger module universe.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), via its integer-sheaf form; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat) and 06YT; blueprint first paragraph, extension of coefficients

proof.text: The complex $L_m$ is bounded by Step 4, so apply the forward implication of [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] with ring $A_m$. Together with Step 5 this proves Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ over $A_m$ for $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_r}A_m$. In particular the pro-etale test sheaves in this assertion are arbitrary $A_m$-module sheaves, not only ones of etale origin.

source.place: First paragraph: the finite-Tor condition after extension of coefficients

proof.text: There are only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves of $K_0$. For each, choose the finite constructible locally closed stratification in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Repeatedly apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] to obtain one finite stratification $i:S\to T$ refining all of them, using the fibre-product schemes as strata. By [lemma-constructible-of-refines] the restrictions of all these sheaves are finite locally constant. For every stratum, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identify these restrictions with the cohomology of $i^*K_0$. The same exactness shows $i^*K_0$ is bounded.

source.place: Tags 095E and 03RZ, finite common stratification; sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC; homology.tex Tag 010N

proof.text:
On such a stratum, the derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], with the constant-ring and exactness identification of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], gives
$$i^*L_m\cong i^*K_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_r}(A_m)_S.$$
Use [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor] on $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, with coefficient ring $A_r$. This ring is Noetherian: it is finite, so an increasing chain of ideals stabilizes. Both inputs are bounded above with locally constant finite-type cohomology by Step 7 and because $A_m$ is a finite $A_r$-module in degree zero. Hence every cohomology sheaf of $i^*L_m$ is locally constant of finite type over $A_r$, equivalently finite locally constant by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values]. Each local constant value is killed by $\ell^m$, because $i^*L_m$ is an $A_m$-complex. Thus it is an $A_m$-module, and its $A_r$-linear trivialization is automatically $A_m$-linear: lift each scalar through $A_r\twoheadrightarrow A_m$. The same trivializations therefore give finite locally constant $A_m$-values.

source.place: Tag 094H, lemma-locally-constant-tensor-product; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 03RU and 03RW; coefficient quotient action written explicitly

proof.text: Exact pullback commutes with cohomology by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Consequently Step 8 proves that every $\mathcal H^j(L_m)$ restricts to finite locally constant $A_m$-modules on the finite constructible stratification of Step 7. This is [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], so $L_m$ is bounded constructible. The finite-ring equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], applied to $A_m$, makes $C_mL_m$ bounded with intrinsically constructible cohomology, and identifies $L_m$ as its bounded constructible ordinary-etale origin. Step 5 is the specified canonical comparison with the reduction of $K$.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; global finite-stratification criterion for the etale origin

proof.text:
For $r\geq m\geq n$, apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] again to $Q_m$ and $A_m\to A_n$. The derived change-of-rings computation [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] represents the successive reduction by $(Q\otimes_{A_r}A_m)\otimes_{A_m}A_n$. The sheaf tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives an isomorphism of complexes
$$(q\otimes b)\otimes c\longmapsto q\otimes bc,$$
with inverse $q\otimes c\longmapsto(q\otimes1)\otimes c$; $bc$ means the image of $b$ in $A_n$ times $c$. The balancing relations prove the two formulas are well-defined inverse maps, and the differential acts only on $q$, so these are chain maps. These are the derived tensor associators on these K-flat representatives. The coefficient comparisons of Step 5 are induced by inverse image of the tensor maps. Both paths around their associator square send a local pure tensor $(q\otimes b)\otimes c$ to the image of $q$ tensored with $bc$. Equality on pure tensors implies equality on tensor presheaves and on their sheafifications, and hence in the derived category. The comparison and associator are natural in chain maps; the canonical K-flat computation of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] makes them independent of the representative. This proves the required coherence without replacing a derived quotient by an underived quotient of $K_0$.

split_report.summary: Ten-step proof with no new nodes. Reflect Tor amplitude by the existing arbitrary finite-ring comparison, use a bounded flat etale model, compute both quotient extensions on K-flat models, prove constructibility on a finite common stratification using Stacks 094H, and check associator coherence on tensors. No Noetherian hypothesis on the scheme and no flatness of the quotient map are used. Maintainer-reader fix: Step 5 now builds the coefficient comparison termwise from the stated inverse-image tensor isomorphism, instead of reading the termwise form off the construction of the derived tensor-pullback isomorphism.
